findings.title: Remote code execution using `__vite-browser-external` virtual module (GHSA-p4f5-76q4-ffq7)
findings.summary_md: The Vite maintainers published this Critical advisory on 10 November 2026, rating it CVSS v4 9.1 and listing no CVE ID. The resolver embeds URL-derived module IDs in the `__vite-browser-external` and `__vite-optional-peer-dep` virtual modules without escaping, which permits injected imports that bypass the `server.fs` allow list and injected code that Vite evaluates through `new Worker` and `import.meta.glob`. Only apps that expose the dev server with `--host` or `server.host` are affected. Fixed versions are vite 6.4.6, 7.3.8, 8.1.7, 8.2.5 and 8.3.7, plus vite-plus 1.5.1; the Vite 8 fixes depend on Rolldown 1.2.17 or 1.1.7.

findings.title: Vite Dev Server RCE (GHSA-p4f5-76q4-ffq7): One HTTP Request to an Exposed `vite --host` Runs Code on Your Machine
findings.summary_md: TechPulse reported on 11 November 2026 that a crafted HTTP request against a network-reachable Vite dev server can run arbitrary code, while a localhost-only server is not reachable by the attack. It traces the flaw to unescaped URL-derived IDs in the two virtual modules, noting that injected imports make files outside the project readable and that `globalThis.process.getBuiltinModule` bypasses the blocked globals in Vite's evaluation path. The article lists the same patched versions as the advisory and calls out Docker, cloud IDE, devcontainer and CI preview setups as common sources of `--host` exposure. It also warns that transitive Vite copies in frameworks such as Astro, SvelteKit, Nuxt, Vitest and Storybook must be checked in lockfiles.

findings.title: Critical Vite Dev Server Bug: Who Needs to Update Now
findings.summary_md: KrishivLabs published a practitioner advisory on 12 November 2026, describing how an unescaped request-derived module ID lets attacker code into a trusted Vite dev-server module and then reaches execution through the `new Worker` and `import.meta.glob` eval path. It repeats the upstream condition that only `--host` or `server.host` deployments are affected and that built static output is not the vulnerable component. The post recommends `npm ls vite`, upgrading to 6.4.6, 7.3.8, 8.1.7, 8.2.5 or 8.3.7 and vite-plus 1.5.1, and removing network binds until patched. It adds that Vite 4 and 5 have no listed patch in those lines and advises rotating keys exposed on an affected development machine.
